target.description: The template is the Excel format you'll ultimately hand over — its header row determines which columns the output will have.
target.example: For example: a monthly sales report — the header row is the row with "Order ID", "Customer Name", etc.

targetTemplate.definition: The Excel format you'll ultimately hand over

sheet.definition: An Excel file can have multiple tabs; each tab is a sheet

headerRow.definition: The row that contains column names, e.g. the row with "Order ID", "Customer Name"

sources.description: Where your data comes from — you can have multiple source files, exactly one of which is the primary.
sources.example: For example: an orders file (primary) plus a customer lookup file (lookup).

sourceFile.definition: The actual file the data comes from

alias.definition: A short name you choose; joins and mappings refer to this file by this name

primary.definition: The main data processed row by row; other source files are used for lookups

role.definition: A source file's role tag: primary or lookup

joins.description: Only needed when you have multiple source files: tells the system which column in each file represents the same thing (the join key).

join.definition: Tells the system which column in two files represents the same thing, so rows can be matched

mappings.description: Each row here is one output column; the settings on a row decide where that column's value comes from.
mappings.example: For example: add a row, set target to "Customer Name", source to customers.name — the output gets one more column.
mappings.emptyState: No template uploaded yet, so there are no fields to map. Go back to Step 1, or add a row manually.

mapping.definition: For each output column, where its value comes from — a source field or a fixed value

outputColumn.definition: An actual column in the output file; adding/removing a row in mappings adds/removes an output column

sourceField.definition: This column's value is read from a specified source column for each row

literal.definition: Regardless of the source, this column is always filled with the same value

sourceCell.definition: Instead of reading row by row, read directly from one specific cell in the source file, e.g. B2

save.description: This is the last step — check the summary for anything you missed, then enter a name to save and download.
save.example: For example: if you picked the wrong source file, click "Edit" to jump back to Step 2.

target.heading: Target template
target.notUploaded: (not uploaded — re-upload required after restoring from a draft)
